title: Sub-cycle metrology of bright quantum light
summary: In quantum optics, quantization of the electromagnetic field typically occurs in a finite volume - a cavity - which results in discrete frequency modes where photons are created, annihilated and exchanged between such modes. As a result, evolution of quantum optical states is periodic in the carrier wave of the field, measurement protocols return cycle-averaged information, and any sub-cycle evolution that is foundational to many light-matter interactions, especially at high field strengths, remains hidden.
